evals.prompt: Build me an iOS shortcut that asks 'What's your name?', then posts a banner notification 'Hello, <name>!', and finally shows on screen 'Nice to meet you, <name>'. Produce the .shortcut file and prove it passes validation.
evals.expected_output: An unsigned .shortcut (binary plist) built from assets/example-hello.json with ask -> notification -> showresult; {name} wired via token strings with correct UTF-16 offsets; validate_shortcut.py --target ios --min-os 26 reports 0 errors; inspect shows the actions in order; signing on a Mac is stated as the remaining step for iOS 15+ import.

evals.prompt: I downloaded a .shortcut file from GitHub and my iPhone running iOS 17 says "Couldn't add shortcut" when I open it. What is wrong, how do I fix it, and what should I check in the file itself before trying again?
evals.expected_output: Explains iOS 15+ requires signed AEA1 files: sign on a Mac with `shortcuts sign --mode anyone` (or people-who-know-me) or share via iCloud link from Shortcuts.app; the iOS 13/14 unsigned path with Allow Untrusted Shortcuts (grayed until a shortcut has run once); tells the user to lint the unsigned plist with validate_shortcut.py and inspect it before retrying; mentions a signed AEA1 file cannot be linted directly and the file-name-becomes-shortcut-name rule.

evals.prompt: Take a shortcut that calls an API with Get Contents of URL and make it safe: fetch https://api.example.com/status, read the 'status' key; if it is not 'ok', show an alert 'API failed' with the actual status; otherwise read the 'message' key and show it (prefix the text with an emoji). Give me the new .shortcut and its spec.
evals.expected_output: Spec + built .shortcut (assets/example-api-guard.json) with download -> getdict(status) -> conditional WFCondition 5 (is not, string compare 'ok' via WFConditionalActionString, GroupingIdentifier g1) -> alert -> else -> getdict(message) -> showresult with emoji + {placeholders} -> endif; builder/linter report balanced control flow and 0 errors; token-string offsets are UTF-16 correct (the emoji counts as 2 code units).

evals.prompt: My shortcut works on my Mac but does nothing on my iPhone. Here is the file: examples/broken-post-clipboard.shortcut. Diagnose it and give me a version that works on iOS.
evals.expected_output: Runs the target-diff: validate --target ios reports 6 errors vs 5 on macos, isolating E_MACOS_ONLY (runshellscript) as the platform bug; also names E_COND_NO_INPUT, E_COND_LITERAL (code 99 needs WFConditionalActionString), E_INPUT_KEY (text.replace carrying 'text'), E_MATH_OP (ASCII '/'), and E_UNCLOSED_GROUP (g1 never closes) as design bugs; notes fix_shortcut.py repairs only the provable subset and refuses to write; delivers the corrected rebuild from examples/post-clipboard.json (changecase instead of shell, condition 100 existence guard, closed if/else/endif, visible output) linting 0 errors on ios, plus the Mac signing step. Does not claim the unsigned file imports on iOS 15+.

evals.prompt: I have no Mac — I am on Windows. Make me a shortcut that opens the first link in my clipboard and get it onto my iPhone.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT promise an importable .shortcut (iOS 15+ imports signed files only; only macOS signs) and says so early. Builds examples/open-first-url.json on Windows (getclipboard -> detectlinks -> if condition 100 -> firstitem -> openurl, else alert), lints 0 errors for --target ios, inspects the action list, then delivers the honest hand-off: a numbered Shortcuts.app build recipe and/or the unsigned file plus the one-line `shortcuts sign --mode anyone` command for any borrowed Mac, or an iCloud-link path once it exists on a device.

evals.prompt: Here is a .shortcut whose variables look wrong: the 'age' value shows up where the 'name' should be. The file imports fine and the editor shows no error. Can you repair it?
evals.expected_output: Understands that a token string's attachmentsByRange key order carries no meaning, and that the bug is a swapped attachment rather than a bad offset. Uses fix_shortcut.py, which keeps every attachment bound to the placeholder it already occupies and only moves an attachment whose offset is not a placeholder — never re-binding positionally, which is what caused the swap. Explains that an ambiguous token string (two or more unanchored attachments) is deliberately left alone and still reported as E_TOKEN_RANGE, and that the agent must not hand-patch a binary plist but change the spec, rebuild and re-lint. Does NOT claim a repaired file is importable on iOS 15+ without signing.

evals.prompt: Build me a shortcut that reads a URL from the clipboard, POSTs the clipboard contents as a JSON body, and shows the response. Put the API key in a variable.
evals.expected_output: Builds from a spec where the download's extra parameters carry the request body, and the body resolves to a real WFTextTokenString with an attachment rather than literal {name} text — the spec layer promotes the {"Value": "..."} shape and resolves placeholders recursively. Wires the API key as a variable rather than a hardcoded secret (see SECURITY.md). Lints 0 errors for --target ios, inspects the action list, and states that iOS 15+ import needs a signed file from a Mac.
